title: Accounting and Tax Services for House Flippers

rows.before: We complete a section 85 rollover on Form T2057 to move a property you hold personally into the flipping corporation at an elected amount, deferring the business income a straight sale of that property inventory would trigger, so incorporating mid-project on a $600,000 flip creates no immediate CRA liability.
rows.after: We complete a section 85 rollover on Form T2057 to move a property you hold personally into the flipping corporation at an elected amount, deferring the business income a straight sale of that property inventory would trigger, so incorporating mid-project on a $600,000 flip creates no immediate CRA liability.
rows.note: $600,000 here is the value of a flip property, not the small business limit; R7 does not apply. Leave as is.

rows.before: We established that a fix-and-flip corporation earns active business income — an adventure in the nature of trade — not property income, restated the flips to 100% business income under section 9 on amended T2 returns, and claimed the section 125 small business deduction so the first $500,000 was taxed at 12.2%.
rows.after: We established that a fix-and-flip corporation earns active business income — an adventure in the nature of trade — not property income, restated the flips to 100% business income under section 9 on amended T2 returns, and claimed the section 125 small business deduction so the first $500,000 was taxed at 11.2% (12.2% before July 1, 2026).
rows.note: Case-study result stated without a date as the current SBD-taxed rate; treated as current. If Sharad dates this engagement before July 1, 2026, switch to R3 (leave).

rows.before: Captured the $500,000 small business deduction at 12.2%
rows.after: Captured the $500,000 small business deduction at 11.2%
